notes.title: My, your, his
notes.body: Put in, a or u in front of a word to say whose it is.

quotes.es: Este pronombre se llama mixto, porque igualmente sirve para demostrativos y posesivos.
quotes.en: This pronoun is called mixed because it serves equally as demonstrative and possessive.

quotes.es: En cuanto posesivo sirve para declinar todos los nombres, que así mismo comienzan en consonante.
quotes.en: As a possessive it serves to decline all nouns that likewise begin with a consonant, but only when denoting possession.
There are two forms of the pronoun, the real pronoun called "verbal" and used as a suffix and the possessive pronoun called "nominal" and used as a prefix.

notes.title: Counting people and things
notes.body: A number never stands alone. Add -tul to count people, -pel to count things.

quotes.en: There is a large number of classificatory suffixes in use with the numerals. The latter can never stand alone.
At the present time all nouns are broadly classified into two classes, animate and inanimate, by the two suffixes -tul and -p'el:
oš-tul winik, three men, — oš-p'el na, three houses.
oš la hun, 13 (3 and 10). — kan la hun, 14 (4 and 10), etc.
These latter show, in most cases, a fleshless lower jaw signifying 10 in addition to the glyph for the numbers from 3 to 9.

notes.title: Whose son?
notes.body: Say the thing first, with u. Then say whose it is.

quotes.en: The forms of the nominal pronoun used to convey the idea of possession are attached to the name of the object possessed rather than to that of the possessor;
u peq winik, the man's dog.

dict.es: AL: hijo ó hija de la mujer; así llama tambien á los de su hermana; por lo regular va unido á las letras eufónicas u, y, como ual para el hijo propio, yal para el ajeno.
dict.en: AL: son or daughter of a woman; she also calls her sister's children so. It is usually joined to the euphonic letters u, y, as ual for one's own child, yal for another's.

glyph.says: Eb, a day sign in the Dresden Codex: a face in profile.
Kan, a day sign in the Dresden Codex. Pío Pérez gives kan as yellow.
Manik, a day sign in the Dresden Codex: a shape like a hand.

glyph.spelling_ref: wayeb2025 logogram TUN: tuun, stone; spelled tu-ni
glyph.says: This spells tu-ni: tun, stone. Your word tunich means stone too.
glyph.credit: Drawing © David Stuart, used with permission

glyph.says: Five: one bar. Ho in Maya.
Ten: two bars. Lahun in Maya.
Nineteen: three bars and four dots. Bolonlahun in Maya.
Seven: one bar and two dots. Campel catac oxpel: four and three make uucpel.

glyph.spelling_ref: wayeb2025 logogram AL/YAL: (mother's) son; spelled ya-la
glyph.says: This spells ya-la: yal, a woman’s child. Same word as al.
glyph.credit: Drawing © David Stuart, used with permission

glyph.says: Chuen, a day sign in the Dresden Codex: two curls facing each other.
Cimi, a day sign in the Dresden Codex: a closed eye with lashes.
Oc, a day sign in the Dresden Codex. Pío Pérez gives oc as foot and leg: your word oc.
